## 20260515T004946Z-slumbot-torch-levelsync-cuda-integration - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-15T00:49:46Z
- Type: protected integration diagnostic
- Gate: TDD + methodology-review + objective-audit + live smoke
- Hypothesis: The new level-synchronous Torch CUDA resolver should be callable
  from live Slumbot smoke paths explicitly, without changing the default solver
  backend or promotion policy.
- Failure class: compute_integration
- Summary: Extended Slumbot and autoresearch CLI backend choices to accept
  `torch-levelsync-cuda` and `torch-levelsync-cpu`, while leaving `auto` on the
  stable CPU path. Added regression tests for queue forwarding and Slumbot help
  exposure.
- Evidence:
  - Review: `autoresearch-session/poker_reviews/20260515T004500Z-torch-levelsync-cuda-cfr`
  - Tests: `uv run pytest -q test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch.py test/unit/test_slumbot_diagnostics.py test/unit/test_solver_backend.py` -> `67 passed`.
  - Objective audit with review passed for `scripts/play_slumbot.py`,
    `scripts/poker_autoresearch_slumbot.py`, `scripts/poker_autoresearch.py`,
    and the new tests.
  - Live smoke: `uv run python scripts/poker_autoresearch_slumbot.py --model models/slumbot_2p_iter1000.pt --hands 3 --greedy --no-allin --solver-backend torch-levelsync-cuda --timeout-seconds 600` -> passed.
- Metrics: live smoke had `0` API errors, `0` parse errors, `2` solver
  decisions, mean reported solver latency `1270.3 ms`, max `1593.3 ms`, mean
  solver hands `1005.5`, and elapsed `2.031 s/hand`.
- Decision: integration is valid but not promoted. Do not flip `auto` to CUDA
  until mixed turn/river fixed-state parity and live latency attribution show
  that the end-to-end path beats CPU on the same states.

## 20260515T005447Z-resolver-latency-attribution-metrics - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-15T00:54:47Z
- Type: protected evaluation diagnostic
- Gate: TDD + methodology-review + related-work check + objective-audit
- Hypothesis: Separating inner CFR recurrence latency from resolver setup
  overhead will explain why the CUDA level-sync recurrence does not fully
  translate into live Slumbot latency.
- Failure class: compute_integration
- Related work: GPU-CFR supports coarse matrix/vector boundaries for GPU
  acceleration; DeepStack supports end-to-end continual resolving latency as
  the relevant online boundary. Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.14778,
  https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.01724, and
  https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28254783/.
- Summary: Added per-case and aggregate latency attribution to the fixed
  resolver benchmark: total solver path, `StreetSolver.solve(...)` CFR
  recurrence time, and residual setup overhead.
- Evidence:
  - Review: `autoresearch-session/poker_reviews/20260515T005447Z-resolver-latency-attribution-metrics`
  - Manifest: `docs/research_protocols/poker_review_manifests/20260515T005447Z-resolver-latency-attribution-metrics.json`
  - CPU artifact: `autoresearch-session/search_consistency_restored200_100x2k_20260513/resolver_benchmark_cpu_iter10_mixed4_attribution_seed20260515.json`
  - CUDA artifact: `autoresearch-session/search_consistency_restored200_100x2k_20260513/resolver_benchmark_torch_levelsync_cuda_iter10_mixed4_attribution_seed20260515.json`
  - Focused test: `uv run pytest -q test/unit/test_resolver_benchmark.py::test_resolver_benchmark_reports_fixed_state_policy_and_solver_metrics` -> `1 passed`.
- Metrics: fixed mixed four-state CFR10 CPU averaged `568.4 ms` total,
  `325.4 ms` CFR, and `243.1 ms` overhead. `torch-levelsync-cuda` averaged
  `329.2 ms` total, `94.0 ms` CFR, and `235.2 ms` overhead.
- Decision: keep the metric as diagnostic instrumentation. The next compute
  target is setup overhead, especially turn equity/payoff matrix and tree
  construction, not another recurrence-only CUDA port.

## 20260515T010338Z-incremental-turn-equity-evaluator - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-15T01:03:38Z
- Type: protected solver performance change
- Gate: TDD + methodology-review + related-work check + objective-audit +
  solver/regression tests + live smoke
- Hypothesis: Precomputing six-card base ranks during turn equity construction
  should avoid redundant five-card subset evaluations and reduce setup
  overhead without changing solver semantics.
- Failure class: compute_integration
- Related work: Cactus Kev-style prime-product lookup evaluators support fast
  five-card rank lookup; this change reuses that local evaluator while avoiding
  redundant best-five-of-seven subset work. Sources:
  https://suffe.cool/poker/evaluator.html and
  https://pokerkit.readthedocs.io/en/0.6/evaluation.html.
- Summary: Added `_evaluate_six_eval_cards` and
  `_evaluate_seven_eval_cards_with_six_base`, then used the incremental path
  inside turn equity matrix construction. Also added direct tests that compare
  the incremental evaluator against the existing full seven-card evaluator.
- Evidence:
  - Review: `autoresearch-session/poker_reviews/20260515T010338Z-incremental-turn-equity-evaluator`
  - Manifest: `docs/research_protocols/poker_review_manifests/20260515T010338Z-incremental-turn-equity-evaluator.json`
  - CPU artifact: `autoresearch-session/search_consistency_restored200_100x2k_20260513/resolver_benchmark_cpu_iter10_mixed4_incremental_eval_seed20260515.json`
  - CUDA artifact: `autoresearch-session/search_consistency_restored200_100x2k_20260513/resolver_benchmark_torch_levelsync_cuda_iter10_mixed4_incremental_eval_seed20260515.json`
  - Tests: `uv run pytest -q test/unit/test_solver_backend.py test/unit/test_resolver_benchmark.py test/unit/test_cfr_budget_frontier.py test/unit/test_solver_update_gate.py` -> `52 passed`.
  - Live smoke: `uv run python scripts/poker_autoresearch_slumbot.py --model models/slumbot_2p_iter1000.pt --hands 3 --greedy --no-allin --solver-backend torch-levelsync-cuda --timeout-seconds 600` -> passed.
- Metrics: fixed mixed four-state CFR10 `torch-levelsync-cuda` improved from
  `329.2 ms` total, `94.0 ms` CFR, `235.2 ms` overhead to `298.4 ms` total,
  `93.2 ms` CFR, `205.2 ms` overhead. CPU improved from `568.4/325.4/243.1 ms`
  to `541.6/326.1/215.5 ms`.
- Decision: keep the optimization. It is a real setup win but not sufficient
  for CUDA auto-promotion; next work should isolate live-only setup costs such
  as range pruning, tree construction, and CPU-to-GPU tensor preparation.

  `924 ms`, but online decision latency was `1571 ms` (`1.7670x` live). Split B

  state features, blueprint/search entropy, margins, or early trace signals,
  then rerun the same root-disjoint gate.

## 2026-05-10 Minimum Raise Parity Fix

- Timestamp: 2026-05-10T18:23:21Z
- Type: audit_fix
- Failure class: action_mapping
- Summary: Slumbot diagnostics showed live action-mapping drift for under-minimum fractional raises. CPU full-deck, fast-state, CUDA, Slumbot play, and range-tracker legal masks now require each fractional raise bucket to meet the no-limit minimum raise contribution before it is legal.
- Verification: `pytest -q test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch_eval.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch_slumbot.py test/unit/test_slumbot_diagnostics.py test/unit/test_network_mask.py test/unit/test_slumbot_mapping.py test/unit/test_legal_mask_parity.py`; `/usr/bin/env NUMBA_ENABLE_CUDASIM=1 python scripts/test_feature_encoding.py`; direct CUDA-sim legal-mask probe.

## 2026-05-10 GPU Training Readiness Fix

- Timestamp: 2026-05-10T18:36:07Z
- Type: audit_fix
- Failure class: compute_bottleneck
- Summary: Numba CUDA compilation failed because NVVM was not discoverable from the active Python env. Installed `nvidia-cuda-nvcc-cu12==12.6.85`, added the missing `libnvvm.so.4` compatibility symlink, and added `scripts/cuda_env.py` so GPU scripts set `CUDA_HOME` plus `NUMBA_FORCE_CUDA_CC=8.6` inside Python before importing Numba.
- Verification: `pytest -q test/unit/test_cuda_env.py test/unit/test_train_slumbot_args.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch_eval.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch_slumbot.py test/unit/test_slumbot_diagnostics.py test/unit/test_network_mask.py test/unit/test_slumbot_mapping.py test/unit/test_legal_mask_parity.py`; one-iteration Slumbot GPU training smoke saved `models/autoresearch_minraise_smoke/corrected_minraise_final.pt` with `device=cuda`, `traverse=2.3s`, `train=0.6s`.

## 2026-05-10 GPU Replay Cache OOM Fix

- Timestamp: 2026-05-10T18:42:00Z
- Type: audit_fix
- Failure class: compute_bottleneck
- Summary: The 300-iteration corrected-minimum-raise training gate failed at iteration 13 with CUDA OOM after the 10M replay buffer pushed GPU cache usage near the 8GB card limit. Added a memory-budget guard so `_MultiBufferView` skips the GPU replay cache when its estimated tensor footprint would consume too much free GPU memory.
- Verification: `pytest -q test/unit/test_gpu_cache_budget.py test/unit/test_cuda_env.py test/unit/test_train_slumbot_args.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch_eval.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch_slumbot.py test/unit/test_slumbot_diagnostics.py test/unit/test_network_mask.py test/unit/test_slumbot_mapping.py test/unit/test_legal_mask_parity.py`.

## 20260511T140726Z-compact-gpu-replay-cache-reduces-memory-budget - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-11T14:07:26Z
- Type: audit_fix
- Failure class: compute_bottleneck
- Summary: Added compact GPU replay-cache storage for features and advantages, keeping iterations in fp32 and promoting compact advantage targets back to fp32 in the loss path. The GPU trainer now releases traversal workspace before training and releases replay cache after training so PyTorch cached memory does not starve the next Numba traversal. A reuse-budget guard keeps full-cache rebuilds off when the per-iteration training draw is much smaller than the replay buffer.
- Metrics: Compact replay-cache estimate for 20,000,000 samples is 5.104 GiB versus 10.133 GiB with float32 feature/advantage tensors. Direct CUDA probe returned `features=torch.float16`, `advantages=torch.float16`, and `iterations=torch.float32`. A 1,000,000-sample synthetic replay benchmark with 125 batches of 8,192 samples measured 0.235s host fallback versus 0.065s compact cache (`3.629x` faster). A 30-iteration Slumbot-track training benchmark crossed the 20,000,000-sample buffer mark without CUDA OOM and held steady at roughly `traverse=1.6-1.7s`, `train=1.0-1.1s`, `iter=2.8-2.9s` after warmup.
- Verification: `pytest -q test/unit/test_gpu_cache_budget.py test/unit/test_cuda_env.py test/unit/test_train_slumbot_args.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch_eval.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch_slumbot.py test/unit/test_slumbot_diagnostics.py test/unit/test_network_mask.py test/unit/test_slumbot_mapping.py test/unit/test_legal_mask_parity.py`; `/usr/bin/env NUMBA_ENABLE_CUDASIM=1 /home/max/miniconda3/bin/python scripts/test_feature_encoding.py`; `/home/max/miniconda3/bin/python scripts/train_slumbot_2p.py --n-iterations 3 --n-traversals 100 --n-training-steps 50 --buffer-capacity 200000 --hidden-dim 128 --n-layers 2 --batch-size 512 --save-dir models/autoresearch_compact_cache_smoke_20260511T1401Z --prefix compact_cache_smoke --eval-every 0 --save-every 0`; `/home/max/miniconda3/bin/python scripts/train_slumbot_2p.py --n-iterations 30 --n-traversals 800 --n-training-steps 500 --buffer-capacity 10000000 --hidden-dim 512 --n-layers 4 --batch-size 2048 --save-dir models/autoresearch_compact_cache_benchmark_20260511T1416Z --prefix compact_cache --eval-every 0 --save-every 0`.

## 20260513T071538Z-leaf-cache-error-attribution - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-13T07:15:38Z
- Type: workflow
- Gate: manual-leaf-cache-error-attribution
- Hypothesis: Before building another learned-leaf mechanism, cached exact leaf labels should expose whether high-drift errors are broad or concentrated in specific terminal action families.
- Failure class: search_integration
- Related work: DeepStack and Supremus support depth-limited continual resolving with learned counterfactual value networks (https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.01724 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.10442), while ReBeL and Student of Games point toward public-belief-state search/value learning rather than single-state action distillation (https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.13544 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03178). Safe/nested subgame solving also warns that imperfect-information subgames depend on the broader strategy context, so leaf replacement must be evaluated through search behavior, not only per-hand MAE (https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.02955).
- Summary: Added `scripts/analyze_dual_cfv_cache_errors.py`, which loads an existing exact dual-CFV cache, optionally merges leaf-export metadata by label, derives structural fields such as action shape and bet count, and groups model errors/residuals without re-solving. A feasibility check showed one exact river leaf label still costs about `9.0s` even with one CFR iteration, so a full exact-leaf oracle callback for the `0128` case would require thousands of solver calls and is not practical. Cache attribution shows the high-drift model is not failing uniformly: the worst MAE group is `ck/b200c/b150b525c/` at `0.1840`, while `ck/b200c/b150b712c/` has the largest residual miss at `0.1192`; simple call-through `ck/b200c/b150c/` is lowest at `0.1422` MAE and `0.0619` residual miss. On the broader 50-state rotated holdout, error increases with terminal betting complexity: bet-count `0`/`1`/`2` MAE is `0.1805`/`0.2003`/`0.2423`, while bet-count `4`/`5`/`6` is `0.3558`/`0.4175`/`0.5234`. Zero-sum projection removes predicted residual by construction but keeps the high-drift worst group near the same MAE (`0.1815`), so the next mechanism should target richer continuation values and terminal/bet-structure coverage rather than projection or uncertainty gates.

## 20260513T103441Z-successor-frontier-reach-shift - failed

Completing the full root-disjoint high-bet train pool produced `119` cuts, but the same three holdout shapes remained absent and the model still failed (`MAE/RMSE 0.3653/0.4657` vs best constant `0.3184/0.3935`). This falsifies early target truncation as the main explanation. The next principled step is not another small MLP or filter; it should build a broader successor-frontier pool/split that explicitly audits action-shape and reach coverage before training, or move to a range-conditioned residual objective.

Next work should avoid hard value substitution and test safer integration: calibrated residual values, value mixing/warm-start priors, uncertainty-aware cut selection, or direct policy/value training at the resolver action boundary.

- Type: experiment

- Hypothesis: A calibrated policy-head distribution can serve as a soft prior to improve a cheap low-iteration resolver relative to a stronger reference solver, without directly selecting the network argmax.
- Failure class: search_integration
- Summary: Added `scripts/eval_policy_prior_solver_budget.py` to compare three distributions on the same fixed cases: low-budget solver, policy-head-only, and a fixed `0.25` mixture of low-budget solver plus policy head, all measured against a `25`-iteration solver reference. On the `64` held-out policy cases, the `5`-iteration solver was already closer to the `25`-iteration reference than the soft prior mix: mean L1 `0.5778` for low solver versus `0.5950` for the mix. Mixed action agreement did not improve (`0.5469`, same as low solver), and the all-in top-action rate stayed at `0.6563`. The calibrated policy alone was farther from the reference (`0.8097` L1). This falsifies naive final-distribution mixing as a useful policy prior. A real prior must enter the CFR update/warm-start mechanism or be trained against low-vs-high solver residual behavior, not mixed after the solve.

- Failure class: transfer_gap
- Summary: Ran stochastic policy-head local smoke against random and duplicate-swapped head-to-head against the base restored checkpoint. The small random-opponent smoke was positive on average (`+166.1 chips/hand`) but had negative lower95 (`-62.1`). Next mechanism should either train all-street policy targets or evaluate a mixed path that uses regret/blueprint for unsupported early streets and the calibrated stochastic policy head only where search targets exist.

This supports action-boundary auxiliary supervision as the next diagnostic path, not gameplay promotion.

- Hypothesis: If the root-policy auxiliary failed because each exact public-state solve produced only one sampled private-hand policy target, then exporting every legal private hand's exact root strategy from the same solve should reduce all-in collapse and improve held-out root-policy distribution fit.
- Failure class: partial_distribution_transfer

The next mechanism should evaluate the learned distribution as a soft or stochastic search prior on a fresh held-out slice, not lower thresholds on this one.

## 20260513T173500Z-compute-bottleneck-not-established - note

- Timestamp: 2026-05-13T17:35:00Z
- Type: interpretation
- Gate: manual-research-log-correction
- Hypothesis: The current search-consistency failures should not be attributed to insufficient personal-PC compute until profiling demonstrates that the GPU/training pipeline is saturated and that available acceleration paths have been exhausted.
- Failure class: unproven_compute_bottleneck
- Related work: DeepStack/ReBeL show that strong poker systems can be bottlenecked by public-belief target generation and search-aligned training data, but they do not justify treating compute as the blocker before measuring utilization. Their core lesson for this project is to learn the solver-compatible object on the resolver distribution, then scale the proven path.
- Summary: The current evidence points first to target/search-interface mismatch: static successor CFV targets, dynamic cut targets, dense all-hand root-policy distillation, and naive policy warm-starts all failed held-out resolver behavior gates. Compute is not yet a demonstrated blocker. The user observed low GPU utilization, and the workflow has not yet produced a clean profiler report showing sustained GPU saturation, CPU/GPU overlap, dataloader utilization, kernel occupancy, or the effect of modern training settings such as AMP with FP16/BF16 where supported, TF32 matmul, larger batches, fused/compiled training steps, and persistent target-generation workers. Future reports must separate `algorithmic bottleneck` from `systems bottleneck`: before saying local compute is limiting, provide a short profiler-backed A/B showing where wall time goes and whether mixed precision or batching materially changes samples/sec or train sec/iter.
- Metrics file: none; this is a corrective interpretation note based on the failed search-consistency experiments above and the absence of a profiler-backed compute-saturation report.

- Type: diagnostic

- Hypothesis: The next principled step is to falsify both explanations separately: profile whether policy-head training is under-optimized, and attribute held-out policy failure to solver instability, public-root distribution, or model confidence/pathology before adding more research knobs.
- Failure class: partial_systems_underoptimization_and_policy_transfer_gap
- Related work: DeepStack/ReBeL motivate learning search-compatible public-belief objects; Deep CFR motivates average-policy distillation but does not remove the need for held-out public-state generalization. The systems lesson is separate: efficient training matters only after the search target is aligned with the gameplay interface.
- Summary: Added `scripts/profile_joint_pbs_training.py` and `scripts/analyze_joint_pbs_policy_alignment.py` with unit tests. On the exact policy-only joint-PBS artifact from the failed 25-iteration distillation run, a repeat training profile showed the FP32/no-TF32 baseline at `262008` samples/sec with only `48.0%` average sampled GPU utilization. TF32 improved to `305239` samples/sec (`1.165x`), AMP FP16 to `471340` (`1.799x`), AMP BF16 to `495340` (`1.891x`), and AMP FP16 with batch `16384` to `616427` (`2.353x`) with `96.75%` average sampled GPU utilization and `4633 MiB` peak allocated memory. The 5-vs-25 iteration exact solver comparison had top-1 `0.765625`, mean L1 `0.525374`, and model-error correlation to low/high solver disagreement only `-0.0924`, so the worst model errors are not mainly solver-budget instability. They are overconfident action/all-in transfer errors on unseen public roots.

## 20260513T183500Z-root-split-leakage-policy-transfer - failed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-13T18:35:00Z
- Type: diagnostic
- Gate: manual-root-split-leakage-debug
- Hypothesis: The apparent internal policy-distillation fit is inflated because the split is row-disjoint but not public-root-disjoint; all-hand policy targets create many private-hand rows per public root, so a row split validates on public roots already seen during training.
- Failure class: validation_leakage_public_root_generalization
- Related work: Public-belief search systems such as DeepStack/ReBeL require generalization over public states, not just over private hands within an already-seen public state. A split that shares public roots measures the wrong quantity for gameplay search integration.
- Summary: Audited the failed 25-iteration policy-only dataset and found that the original train/internal-holdout split had `128` train roots, `128` holdout roots, and `128` overlapping roots. It split private-hand rows inside each public root, not public roots. This explains the misleading internal score (`0.279322` L1, `0.8353` top-1): the model was tested on seen public roots. Added optional `--group-field root_label` support to `scripts/split_joint_pbs_by_metadata.py` plus a regression test enforcing root-disjoint train/holdout groups. Re-splitting the same `128`-root policy-only target set with `--group-field root_label` produced `96` train roots, `32` holdout roots, and `0` root overlap. Retraining the same `96x32` joint-PBS policy head on this corrected split dropped holdout performance to `0.847682` L1 and `0.551668` top-1, despite still beating legal-uniform L1 (`0.997732`). This identifies the main recurring misalignment cause: the old internal validation measured hand-level interpolation within seen public roots, while gameplay requires public-root extrapolation. Legal-uniform-only pass criteria are too weak for root-policy promotion.

## 20260513T190500Z-low-solver-residual-rootdisjoint - failed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-13T19:05:00Z
- Type: experiment
- Gate: manual-low-solver-conditioned-residual
- Hypothesis: If direct high-budget policy distillation fails because the model is trying to learn the full search distribution from public features alone, then conditioning on a cheap 5-iteration resolver policy and learning only a residual correction to the 25-iteration target should improve true public-root-disjoint holdout behavior.
- Failure class: residual_policy_transfer_gap
- Related work: ReBeL/DeepStack-style systems use search at decision time and learned networks at search-compatible interfaces; a residual-to-cheap-search target is more aligned with that interface than replacing search with a standalone cloned policy. Strategy warm-start work also suggests that learned policy information must be calibrated before it is injected into search.
- Summary: Made root-disjoint evaluation mandatory in `eval_joint_pbs_continuation_probe.py` whenever train/holdout metadata expose `root_label`, with `--allow-root-overlap` reserved for diagnostics. Added `scripts/train_joint_pbs_low_solver_residual.py`, which solves each public root once with a cheap low-iteration resolver, uses that strategy as base logits, and trains a neural delta toward the high-budget all-hand policy target. On the corrected 96-train-root / 32-holdout-root split, low-solver coverage was complete (`108288` train rows and `36096` holdout rows filled; no skipped roots). The cheap 5-iteration solver itself was much stronger than the direct root-disjoint cloned policy: holdout L1 `0.488658`, KL `0.238154`, top-1 `0.781056`. This suggests the immediate blocker is not just neural capacity; the correction target needs calibration/uncertainty structure or direct integration into search, rather than another unconstrained policy head.

ReBeL reinforces training/search on public belief states and recursive solving; PyStack shows the DeepStack-style continual resolving/value-network interface (`ContinualResolving`, `Resolving`, `Lookahead`, `NextRoundValue`); Deep CFR remains relevant for average-strategy baselines but is not the right integration surface for this failure. ## 20260513T203000Z-callback-state-dcvn-smoke - partial

- Timestamp: 2026-05-13T20:30:00Z
- Type: experiment
- Gate: manual-callback-state-dcvn-smoke
- Hypothesis: If the DCVN leaf failure is caused by training on root public states while search queries deeper callback leaf states with dynamic CFR reaches, then training dual-CFV values on the actual callback-state distribution should improve held-out leaf substitution behavior.
- Failure class: partial_callback_state_alignment
- Related work: DeepStack/PyStack and ReBeL both imply that learned values should be trained on the same public-belief state distribution where recursive solving queries them. This experiment tests that interface directly instead of adding another root-policy clone or capacity sweep.
- Summary: Added `scripts/build_public_belief_callback_leaf_targets.py`, which runs the CPU street solver with a non-mutating `showdown_leaf_fn`, records the exact callback states queried during CFR, converts default CFR numerator values back into per-hand EV labels using reach denominators, and saves a dual-CFV cache compatible with the existing trainer. Built a small train cache from roots `0..3` (`2048` kept callback states from `4140` seen) and a root-disjoint holdout cache from roots `128..131` (`1773` kept from `3276` seen). A tiny deepset dual-CFV checkpoint trained on these callback states beat zero/train-mean MAE but not train-mean RMSE, so the supervised checkpoint gate remained failed. However, when evaluated as a learned leaf on the same root-disjoint holdout slice, it passed the small diagnostic A/B: unprojected leaf substitution reached `0.50` action agreement and `0.3551` mean L1 drift; projected substitution reached `0.75` action agreement and `0.3977` mean L1 drift. This is the strongest evidence so far that distribution alignment, not merely model size, is the main DCVN integration issue. It is still only a 4-root smoke and is not promotable.

## 20260515T071500Z-corrected-pool-telemetry-ab - failed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-15T07:15:00Z
- Type: traversal_fidelity_ab_diagnostic
- Gate: telemetry-enabled default-vs-1000 slot comparison
- Hypothesis: Increasing per-traversal slots may create a good enough
  corrected-semantics training point without changing the algorithm.
- Failure class: traversal_fidelity_and_throughput_tradeoff
- Related work: Deep CFR uses external-sampling MCCFR and explores all actions
  at traverser infosets; MCCFR is unbiased because sampled regrets are
  corrected by the sampling scheme. Sources:
  https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/brown19b/brown19b.pdf,
  https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/3713-monte-carlo-sampling-for-regret-minimization-in-extensive-games,
  and
  https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/4569-efficient-monte-carlo-counterfactual-regret-minimization-in-games-with-many-player-actions.
- Summary: Reran 3-iteration corrected-semantics CUDA probes with the new JSON
  telemetry. The fast default was badly under-fidelity: every chunk overflowed,
  mean pool demand was `3.98x`, and max demand was `8.38x`, although throughput
  was `367` traversals/sec. Raising slots to 1000 reduced mean demand to
  `1.76x` and max to `2.73x`, but every chunk still overflowed and throughput
  fell to `230` traversals/sec. The CUDA fork kernel currently demotes
  traverser nodes to sampled actions on pool exhaustion; that is a practical
  fallback, not a principled MCCFR sampling scheme.
- Commands: `uv run python scripts/poker_autoresearch_train.py --n-iterations 3 --n-traversals 4000 --n-training-steps 20 --hidden-dim 512 --n-layers 4 --batch-size 8192 --buffer-capacity 2000000 --save-dir autoresearch-session/corrected_allin_pool_telemetry_default_20260515 --prefix corrected_pool_default_3x4k --save-every 0 --eval-games 0`; `uv run python scripts/poker_autoresearch_train.py --n-iterations 3 --n-traversals 4000 --n-training-steps 20 --hidden-dim 512 --n-layers 4 --batch-size 8192 --buffer-capacity 2000000 --traversal-slots-per-traversal 1000 --save-dir autoresearch-session/corrected_allin_pool_telemetry_1000_20260515 --prefix corrected_pool1000_3x4k --save-every 0 --eval-games 0`
- Key metrics: `{"default_traversals_per_second": 367.371, "default_overflow_fraction": 1.0, "default_mean_pool_demand_ratio": 3.980049, "default_max_pool_demand_ratio": 8.375957, "slot1000_traversals_per_second": 229.765, "slot1000_overflow_fraction": 1.0, "slot1000_mean_pool_demand_ratio": 1.758695, "slot1000_max_pool_demand_ratio": 2.727944, "promotion": false}`
- Decision: Do not solve corrected traversal by more slot sweeps. The next
  principled direction is an algorithmic one: either stream full external
  sampling without fixed-pool demotion, or implement a published sampled-action
  MCCFR variant with proper importance weighting/variance controls.

## 20260515T114500Z-without-replacement-sampled-traversal - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-15T11:45:00Z
- Type: traversal_level_estimator_probe
- Gate: PPS without-replacement sampled-action estimator and tiny traversal
  check
- Hypothesis: Sampling traverser actions without replacement should avoid
  duplicate child evaluations, lower estimator variance, and preserve root
  action ordering better than the with-replacement sample-4 probe.
- Failure class: none
- Summary: Added exact inclusion-probability computation for the 9-action
  abstraction, a PPS without-replacement sampler, a Horvitz-Thompson sampled
  regret estimator, and a `--sampling-mode without-replacement` path for root
  and traversal diagnostics. The hard root estimator gate passed at sample-4
  with lower standard deviation than the with-replacement baseline. The tiny
  traversal probe preserved root top action on two seeds while retaining modest
  per-run speedups. This is still a research-only CPU diagnostic, but it is a
  cleaner candidate for CUDA traversal than with-replacement sample-4.
- Sources: MCCFR sampling framework https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2009/file/00411460f7c92d2124a67ea0f4cb5f85-Paper.pdf; VR-MCCFR baselines https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/4048; without-replacement estimators https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.06043 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.09067

## 20260515T153000Z-sampled-traverser-action-pivot - failed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-15T15:30:00Z
- Type: estimator_protocol_review
- Gate: related-work check plus hard-seed 512-repeat variance check
- Hypothesis: The sample-4 priority-baseline failure might be a finite-sample
  artifact that disappears with more repeats.
- Failure class: estimator_contract_mismatch
- Related work: MCCFR external sampling samples chance/opponent actions while
  enumerating the updating player's legal actions; outcome sampling and
  external sampling both have regret bounds, but directly dropping updating
  player actions at the regret-target node is not the standard external
  sampling contract. Sources:
  https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/3713-monte-carlo-sampling-for-regret-minimization-in-extensive-games,
  https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.03057, and
  https://poker.cs.ualberta.ca/publications/NIPS12.pdf.
- Summary: Searched related MCCFR work and reran the hard seed with `512`
  repeats using the learned priority model as both priority and baseline. Bias
  dropped, but top-action agreement still failed. The method retained only a
  small speedup, so scaling repeats does not rescue the sampled-traverser-action
  direction as an acceleration path.
- Commands: `uv run python scripts/eval_sampled_deep_cfr_traversal_grid.py --seeds 20260527 --initial-chips-values 300 --n-repeats 512 --n-reference-repeats 512 --sample-count 4 --sampling-mode priority-without-replacement --priority-forced-count 2 --priority-source priority-model --priority-checkpoint autoresearch-session/restricted_value_baseline_xxl_seed20260524.pt --use-priority-baseline --hidden-dim 64 --n-layers 1 --min-top-match-rate 1.0 --min-mean-speedup 1.05 --max-mean-abs-bias 0.08 --require-all-top-match --max-case-mean-abs-bias 0.08 --output-json autoresearch-session/sampled_deep_cfr_traversal_grid_priority_model_baseline_xxl_f2_sample4_seed20260527_512rep_20260515.json`

## 20260515T111200Z-average-strategy-related-work-check - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-15T11:12:00Z
- Type: related_work
- Gate: Deep CFR / SD-CFR policy-deployment alignment check
- Hypothesis: The live large-pot calibration failure may come from deploying a
  single regret-derived policy rather than the average strategy object that
  Deep CFR theory and SD-CFR variants target.
- Failure class: none
- Summary: Related work supports the diagnosis. Deep CFR trains a separate
  policy network to approximate the weighted average strategy because the
  average strategy, not one iteration's instantaneous regret policy, is the
  equilibrium object. SD-CFR avoids average-policy-network approximation error
  by sampling among stored iteration value networks at trajectory start. ReBeL
  motivates aligning learning and search around public belief state values
  rather than isolated live subgame patches.
- Sources:
  - Deep CFR paper: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/brown19b/brown19b.pdf
  - SD-CFR paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.07621
  - ReBeL / thesis discussion: https://www.csd.cmu.edu/sites/default/files/phd-thesis/CMU-CS-20-132.pdf
- Local check: `scripts/eval_sd_cfr_mixture.py` on retry-clean iteration 25/50
  vs incumbent produced mean `+119.7 chips/hand` but lower95 `-480.7`, so the
  tiny available checkpoint mixture is not promotable.
- Decision: Run a bounded GPU Deep CFR candidate with traversal-collected
  average-strategy targets and evaluate with `--strategy-source average-policy`.
  This is more principled than risk caps because it restores the Deep CFR
  deployed-object contract.

- Type: protected diagnostic tooling
- Gate: TDD + revealed-hand Slumbot opponent-action likelihood
- Hypothesis: If poor trace-conditioned Slumbot ranges come from the
  opponent-response model rather than only terminal-card strength, then the
  model should assign low likelihood to the actual Slumbot actions on hands
  where Slumbot reveals its hole cards.
- Failure class: distribution_shift
- Summary: Added `scripts/diagnose_slumbot_trace_action_likelihood.py` and
  `poker_ai/research/slumbot_trace_action_likelihood.py` to score each
  observed Slumbot action under the loaded model for Slumbot's revealed hand,
  using chronological board visibility and the same Slumbot action mapping as
  range tracking. The diagnostic is a measurement surface only; it does not
  alter live play or training.
- Evidence:
  - Trace:
    `autoresearch-session/slumbot_traces/slumbot-candidate-smoke-20260515T113200Z-avg-strategy-candidate-final-noallin-retry.jsonl`
  - Artifact:
    `autoresearch-session/slumbot_trace_cases/20260515T113200Z-avg-strategy-noallin-action-likelihood.json`
- Key metrics: `n_scored_actions=100`, `n_scored_hands=37`,
  `n_skipped_results=13`, and overall
  `mean_log_lift_vs_uniform=-0.2867`. Street slices: preflop `-0.5234`,
  flop `-0.0804`, turn `-0.1026`, river `+0.0148`. Action slices: bets
  `+0.1632`, checks `-0.0460`, calls `-0.7913`. Large absolute pots were
  also negative at `-0.4128`.
- Validation: `uv run pytest -q test/unit/test_slumbot_trace_action_likelihood.py`
  -> 2 passed. Real diagnostic command:
  `uv run python scripts/diagnose_slumbot_trace_action_likelihood.py --checkpoint models/autoresearch_gpu_20260515T111750Z/avg_strategy_candidate_final.pt --strategy-source average-policy --trace autoresearch-session/slumbot_traces/slumbot-candidate-smoke-20260515T113200Z-avg-strategy-candidate-final-noallin-retry.jsonl --device cuda --output autoresearch-session/slumbot_trace_cases/20260515T113200Z-avg-strategy-noallin-action-likelihood.json`.
- Decision: The range failure is not primarily a "Slumbot bets too much" story.
  On this trace, Slumbot bets are above uniform likelihood; the model is
  mainly surprised by calls and, to a lesser extent, checks, especially before

  public-belief calibration objective that explains Slumbot continuation
  actions without hard-coded action patches, then rerun both revealed-hand
  range and action-likelihood diagnostics before any new Slumbot confidence
  spend.
